{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABeh7jvg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhIC9xg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 299, "title": "Replace Graph Editor Save/Load saved with performant Auto Save and session Undo/Redo (single-writer editing)", "body": "## Goal

Make editing a graph **save automatically** and give users **Undo / Redo** instead of the manual **Save** and **Load saved** actions. Editing must remain responsive, changes must be recoverable across navigation/closing, and **only one tab/window may edit the same graph at a time**.

This task covers the Graph Editor for **regular graphs and reusable subgraph definitions**. It is deliberately larger than a button-only UI change.

## Product decisions (agreed)

1. **Auto Save replaces Save**; remove the Save button and its manual-save workflow.
2. **Undo / Redo** are available while the editor is open. **History is in memory for that editor session only**; reopening starts with empty history. Persistent undo/version history is out of scope.
3. Remove **Load saved** from the normal Graph actions menu. An editor should not need a saved-state rollback action for ordinary edits: Undo reverses the actions and the result is auto-saved.
4. **After a successful Auto Save, automatically prepare required model files**, preserving the existing user-facing behavior previously triggered by Save. Preparation is asynchronous; graph editing does not wait for downloads.
5. Auto Save **must not introduce avoidable performance problems**. Design for low overhead and bounded work, including long text edits, node drags and model preparation. **No benchmark/performance measurement requirement in this issue.**
6. Protect edits when navigating away/closing. A pending debounce or asynchronous save must not silently lose user changes. Implement reliable immediate recovery checkpoints, navigation flush and recovery as described below.
7. **Single-writer policy (option A):** only one tab/window can edit a particular graph at a time. Other tabs showing that graph are read-only. Different graphs may be edited concurrently. No automatic multi-writer graph merge or collaborative/CRDT editing in this task.

## UI / interaction requirements

- Put clearly labeled **Undo** and **Redo** controls in the Graph Editor toolbar (disabled when unavailable); support desktop shortcuts: `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` on Windows/Linux and `Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` on macOS. `Ctrl+Y` may additionally map to Redo. **Do not steal native undo/redo from focused input, textarea, select or contenteditable controls**; handle IME composition correctly.
- Remove `#graph-save` and the Graph actions `#graph-load` control. Update help text, notifications, tooltips, error messages, and documentation that still instruct users to press Save / Load saved.
- Show a small unobtrusive but accessible save state such as **Saving… / Saved / Save failed**; display actionable persistent errors and a retry affordance when needed. Separate graph persistence state from model preparation state and the existing Live **Active / earlier graph** warning.
- A secondary tab for an already edited graph opens **read-only** with a concise indication of why editing is unavailable; allow viewing/inspection and safe export, but disable *every* graph mutation (including shortcuts, drag, settings, import/reset, port editing, create-subgraph, and Undo/Redo). Prefer an explicit **Take over / Start editing** action when the lock becomes available, not a silent takeover. Reload the latest persisted state before granting editing.
- Preserve the current graph selection, canvas navigation, accessible keyboard paths, and desktop/narrow-width usability.

## Undo / Redo semantics

- Track user-intent transactions, not render calls: Node add/remove/move, connect/disconnect/reconnect, node settings, text/number fields, input-port count/labels, subgraph interface edits, graph Reset and Import. Include any other editable graph data changed through current editor controls.
- **Group continuous gestures into one history step**: a pointer drag is one undoable move; keyboard motion bursts and continuous typing (including IME) should not create one snapshot per event/character. Preserve logical atomicity, including wire changes caused by node/port deletion.
- Undo reverses the last locally committed edit transaction; Redo reverses Undo. New edits after Undo clear the redo branch. Undoing a previously auto-saved edit is another change to the working graph and **must itself auto-save**.
- History is bounded and memory-only; use a reasonable documented max (e.g. 100 undo transactions), and avoid storing duplicate full-document snapshots on each mousemove/keystroke. No Undo across closing/reopening the editor.
- Do **not** treat external storage updates, model downloads, selection/zoom/pan-only changes, rendering, or auto-save acknowledgements as user Undo steps.
- Special case: **Create Subgraph** currently commits a new shared library entry before the parent replacement is saved. Keep that persisted side effect explicit: Undo of the parent replacement must not silently delete the shared definition (especially if it has gained other references). Define/test consistent parent-graph undo semantics; no accidental destruction of reusable definitions.

## Auto Save / durability

- Route every meaningful editable graph mutation (including those that currently mutate `this.draft` and call `draw()`, and inspector controls that call `updateSetting()`) through a **central change/transaction boundary**. Do not rely on every caller remembering to invoke save.
- Keep UI mutations immediate; coalesce rapid edits with a short debounce and serialize writes. **At most one in-flight save per graph**; after it finishes, persist the newest state if it changed again. Prevent stale async results from overwriting newer drafts/undo operations. Skip identical content/no-op edits. Avoid full graph serialization, validation, synchronous storage writes and whole-UI redraws in hot mousemove/keypress paths where possible.
- **Recovery before final save**: maintain a *session-scoped, graph-ID + base-revision keyed* recoverable draft/checkpoint. Ensure edit transactions can be recovered even if a debounce or async save is interrupted. Do not write/serialize a full large graph on every pointermove or keystroke; checkpoint at appropriate transaction boundaries and ensure any remaining pending changes are synchronously checkpointed during lifecycle events where possible. Checkpoint failures are **visible**, never reported as Saved.
- For app-controlled navigations (Library / Models / Live / editor-to-subgraph / back to parent), flush and **await graph persistence before navigating**; if persist fails, block navigation or preserve an explicitly recoverable draft and tell the user. Preserve the existing parent/subgraph navigation draft safeguards.
- On pagehide/visibility changes or direct tab/window closing, perform the synchronous available checkpoint and best-effort flush; **do not rely on an asynchronous `beforeunload` save to finish**. On reopen, detect and offer to restore any newer, uncommitted recoverable draft safely (do not auto-overwrite a newer saved revision). Clear checkpoints **only after** the relevant revision is confirmed persisted. Handle quota/storage errors or unsupported write capabilities explicitly. As with any browser storage, cannot guarantee survival of a device/storage failure; never promise an impossible 100% guarantee.
- Ensure invalid/intermediate numeric/text drafts, structurally incomplete graphs, unavailable dependencies and invalid saved graphs do not overwrite a last-known-good version. Preserve/edit/export recoverable drafts, surface validation errors, and retry Auto Save once a draft is valid. Maintain existing graph format/version, library migration and recovery guarantees.
- Avoid `beforeunload` warnings for successfully saved/recoverable edits; warn if the latest changes cannot safely be persisted or recovered.
- Do not silently mark the graph Saved while a write failed, a newer draft is pending, or the saved version is stale.

## Model preparation (triggered by successful Auto Save)

- Preserve the current Save-triggered `preparation.replace(resolvedEntryGraph(...))` behavior **after successful persistence**, but decouple it from the editing/UI critical path.
- Reuse the existing `graphModelStatus` / model-cache preparation code. Deduplicate by *resolved model requirements / asset identity*, rather than initiating new downloads just because a text field changed, a node moved, Undo happened, or a new library revision was written.
- Avoid overlapping/obsolete preparation runs. Coalesce to current requirements; safely cancel or supersede obsolete requests and use verified cached files. Preparation failures show in model-status UI and do **not** roll back a successfully persisted graph.
- If the editor closes while model preparation is in progress, graph data remains saved. Downloads may be interrupted; opening Graph Editor/Models again should be able to resume/check/prepare as appropriate. Do not block closing just to wait for a large download.
- Keep Live's explicit runtime model readiness/ownership semantics unchanged; active sessions keep their immutable snapshot until stopped.

## Single-writer coordination

- Use a **per-graph editing lease/lock** separate from the short-lived `GraphLibrary` storage transaction lock (currently `processing-graph-save`). A Web Lock held for the lifetime of editable Graph Editor would be suitable in MV3; **never hold the library-wide save lock while the editor is open**.
- Acquire the edit lock *before* enabling mutations or autosaves, including existing restored drafts. Lock by stable graph ID so same-graph windows conflict but different graphs do not. Release on editor disposal/navigation/close and let browser lock release on crash; avoid orphaned permanent locks.
- Second viewer for the same graph is read-only. Upon intentional edit acquisition after lock release, reload persisted graph+revision, reject stale unsaved local state from silently overwriting it, initialize a fresh session history, then enable editing.
- Preserve per-entry revision checks and the existing global library write-lock / stale-revision safeguards as a **defense in depth**. Other paths (Graph Library metadata rename, import, legacy recovery, dependency edits, older tabs/extensions) can still update storage. Never overwrite an externally changed graph silently; surface a safe recovery flow (reload latest, or export/duplicate local recoverable draft), not the normal `Load saved` menu action.
- No implicit automatic merge. Edits to *different* graphs must remain possible from independent tabs; check that existing subgraph-reference compatibility validation is not bypassed.

## Main implementation touchpoints

- [`extension/graph-editor.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-editor.js): toolbar and actions, central draft/history transactions, drag/keyboard/input/edit operations, save-state UI, Undo/Redo shortcuts and readonly guarding.
- [`extension/graph-page.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-page.js): per-graph edit lease, serialized Auto Save queue, recovery checkpoint lifecycle, model preparation after save, navigation and cross-tab storage-update handling.
- [`extension/graph-library.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-library.js): keep atomic revision-checked graph persistence and serialized library mutations; extend only as necessary. Preserve graph/subgraph/legacy safety.
- [`extension/graph.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph.css), [`extension/graph-editor.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-editor.html), and help/docs [`docs/extension-graph.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/extension-graph.md): layout/status/help.
- Tests to update/create include [`tests/extension/graph.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/tests/extension/graph.spec.js), [`tests/extension/graph-actions.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/tests/extension/graph-actions.spec.js), [`tests/extension/graph-concurrent.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/tests/extension/graph-concurrent.spec.js), [`tests/extension/subgraphs.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/tests/extension/subgraphs.spec.js), and model-preparation/runtime tests. Numerous specs currently click `#graph-save` or `#graph-load`; migrate them to await the observed autosave/status and persisted revision, not arbitrary sleeps.

## Acceptance criteria / tests

- [ ] No manual Save or Load saved controls/instructions remain in normal Graph Editor UI. Existing graph edits persist automatically with truthful Saving/Saved/Save failed status.
- [ ] Undo/Redo controls and shortcuts work for all supported graph mutations; one drag and one continuous text edit form one logical undo step; native text undo and IME are not hijacked.
- [ ] Undo after a completed Auto Save persists the reverted graph, and Redo persists the re-applied change; new edits clear redo. Reopening starts with no session history.
- [ ] Rapid sequences/long typing/movement do not spawn unbounded writes or model preparations; no duplicate saves for no-op edits; no measurement/benchmark required.
- [ ] Clicking Library/Models/Live or editor-to-subgraph navigation cannot silently lose the final edit. Forced page closure with a pending debounce recovers the pending draft on next open; failed/quota-denied save provides explicit recovery and export.
- [ ] Auto Save completion initiates missing required model preparation without blocking editing. Cached/same requirements do not repeatedly download; requirements changed during preparation are handled safely; model failure does not undo graph persistence.
- [ ] With two tabs on the **same** graph, exactly one can edit at a time. The second is read-only; after the first closes/releases, acquisition reads the newest persisted graph and enables a new history. Two tabs on **different** graphs can edit simultaneously.
- [ ] External revisions, legacy changes, invalid saved graphs, subgraph dependencies and stale restored drafts cannot be silently overwritten; the existing recovery/export path remains available.
- [ ] Live runtime/preload semantics, storage schema, library metadata edits and editor accessibility remain intact.
- [ ] Update automated tests (including existing manual-Save/Load-saved specs) and document exact results in the implementing PR.

## Out of scope

- Persistent undo history, rollback across sessions, version history.
- CRDT/OT, auto-merge, simultaneous editable instances of the same graph.
- Performance benchmarking/profiling.
- Changing model architecture, storage schema or core inference behaviors just for this UI/task.
